brief.headline: Claude Code 2.1.222 fixes worktree/hook bypass — update tonight
brief.summary:
The fix that matters most sits right in the setup you already run: Claude Code 2.1.222 patches worktree-isolated sessions letting subagents run destructive git commands against your main checkout, and fixes PreToolUse auto-allow hooks getting bypassed on background agent tasks. Both bugs were live in the exact worktree-plus-hooks overnight configuration you depend on, so update before your next unattended run. Pair it with David Crawshaw's nightly cron pattern — fetch upstream, rebase, verify it still works, replace the current version — as a concrete template for the kind of run he does unattended.

On the verification side, two repos (fablize, fable-method) both distill Anthropic's internal "Fable" workflow into a portable Think/Act/Prove skill that forces evidence and self-checking before an agent can call a task done — worth trying as the thing that stands between a finished diff and a reviewable PR. Separately, a cluster of cost-routing tools landed at once: opencodex and dao-code let you point routine subagent work at Ollama or DeepSeek-V4's cache-cheap pricing, AirLLM and Homebench let you actually test a 70B model on a 4GB GPU before trusting it, and claudexor rotates across your Claude/Codex subscriptions so a long run doesn't die mid-way on a quota wall.
bullets: Update to Claude Code 2.1.222 now — fixes worktree git-destruction bug and PreToolUse hook bypass on background agents
Run David Crawshaw's cron prompt nightly: fetch upstream, rebase your changes, verify it works, replace the current version
Install fivetaku/fablize or drop Sahir619/fable-method's Think/Act/Prove skill in to force evidence before an agent marks a task done
Point lidge-jun/opencodex or tigicion/dao-code at Ollama or DeepSeek-V4 for routine subagent work instead of Claude-tier pricing
Use razzant/claudexor to auto-rotate across Claude/Codex subscriptions so overnight runs survive a quota wall
Add DietrichGebert/ponytail's rules as a skill to keep agent diffs small enough to actually review each morning

signals.label: Unattended-run reliability
signals.note: Claude Code shipped a targeted fix for worktree/hook bugs that directly broke overnight isolation, alongside two independent repos (fablize, fable-method) adding forced self-verification before completion

signals.label: Cheap/local backend routing
signals.note: opencodex, dao-code, AirLLM, Homebench and a Kimi/GLM scaling writeup all landed this cycle as concrete ways to move routine subagent work off metered frontier APIs

signals.label: Quota walls as a failure mode
signals.note: claudexor exists specifically to auto-rotate subscriptions before a long run hits a quota ceiling, implying this is a common way overnight sessions die

signals.label: Away-from-desk control
signals.note: omnigent and hoplite offer remote/cloud harness paths but neither comes with a failure report or concrete setup detail yet

items.tldr: Claude Code 2.1.222 fixes worktree-isolated sessions letting subagents run destructive git commands against the main checkout, and fixes PreToolUse auto-allow hooks bypassing restrictions on background agent tasks.
items.whyItMatters: These two bugs sat directly in the worktree-plus-hooks setup his unattended overnight workflow depends on — this is a real disclosed breakage, not a spec update.
items.tryThis: Update to Claude Code 2.1.222 now if you run worktree-isolated sessions or background agents behind hook restrictions.

items.title: fivetaku/fablize — A Claude Code plugin that makes Opus behave like Fable — completion, evidence, and verification enforced as procedure. Ships only what a Fable-vs-Opus comparison proved transferable.
items.tldr: Fablize is a Claude Code plugin that forces Opus through a completion/evidence/verification procedure before it can call a task done, shipping only behaviors a Fable-vs-Opus comparison proved actually transferable.
items.whyItMatters: Directly targets 'describe the work, go to sleep, review a finished PR' by making the agent prove its own work before finishing.
items.tryThis: Install the fablize Claude Code plugin and run it on your next overnight task to get enforced evidence/verification before completion.

items.title: Quoting David Crawshaw's prompt
items.tldr: David Crawshaw runs a nightly cron job on the prompt: fetch upstream changes, rebase local changes on top, verify the software still works, then replace the current version — fully unattended.
items.whyItMatters: A minimal, concrete prompt template for exactly the 'describe the work, wake up to a done result' loop you're chasing — apply it to any repo you track upstream on.
items.tryThis: Add a nightly cron entry running your agent on: 'fetch upstream changes to <software>, rebase local changes on top, verify it still works, replace the current version.'

items.title: DietrichGebert/ponytail — Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
items.tldr: Ponytail is a rules/prompt repo that pushes your AI coding agent to write as little code as possible, like a lazy senior dev would.
items.whyItMatters: A drop-in discipline layer against the usual agent failure mode of overbuilding — fewer lines to review in the morning's PR.
items.tryThis: Add ponytail's rules as a skill or system prompt so your agent defaults to the smallest diff instead of gold-plating.

items.title: cobusgreyling/loop-engineering — Practical patterns, starters & CLI tools for loop engineering with AI coding agents. Design systems that prompt and orchestrate agents (inspired by Addy Osmani and Boris Cherny). Includes loop-audit, loop-in
items.tldr: loop-engineering is a repo of CLI tools and patterns for running AI coding agents in loops, shipping loop-audit, loop-init, and loop-cost commands.
items.whyItMatters: These are ready-made CLI primitives for exactly the unattended-agent-loop workflow he's building around Claude Code — loop-cost in particular helps him track what long runs are costing.
items.tryThis: Clone cobusgreyling/loop-engineering and try loop-audit against an existing agent loop to see what it flags.

items.title: lidge-jun/opencodex — Universal provider proxy for OpenAI Codex & Claude Code — use any LLM (Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Ollama…) with Codex CLI, App, SDK, and Claude Code
items.tldr: opencodex is a universal provider proxy letting Codex CLI and Claude Code call any backend — Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, or local Ollama models.
items.whyItMatters: Route routine subagent work to cheap or local models without changing your existing Claude Code/Codex setup.
items.tryThis: Clone lidge-jun/opencodex and point Claude Code's model config at a local Ollama model for routine subagent tasks.

items.title: DenisSergeevitch/agents-best-practices — Provider-neutral Agent Skill for Codex, Claude Code, and agentic harness design.
items.tldr: agents-best-practices packages a provider-neutral Agent Skill for Codex, Claude Code and harness design, at 2,190 stars.
items.whyItMatters: A ready-made skill to standardize subagent behavior instead of writing harness conventions from scratch.
items.tryThis: Install DenisSergeevitch/agents-best-practices as a Skill in your Claude Code project and adapt it to your conventions.

items.title: Sahir619/fable-method — The Fable Workflow: how Claude Fable 5 worked, distilled into skills any model can run, with the eval that keeps it honest. Think / act / prove.
items.tldr: fable-method distills a Think/Act/Prove workflow into portable skills any model can run, plus the eval used to keep the agent honest.
items.whyItMatters: A concrete self-verification pattern to bolt onto agents so they check their own work before you see the PR.
items.tryThis: Clone Sahir619/fable-method and drop its Think/Act/Prove skill and eval into your Claude Code skills folder.

items.title: tigicion/dao-code — Open-source TypeScript terminal coding agent for DeepSeek-V4 — builds on DeepSeek's strong price-performance and ultra-cheap cache pricing, engineering byte-stable prefixes and cache-reusing forks so cross-session memory
items.tldr: dao-code is a TypeScript terminal agent built for DeepSeek-V4, using byte-stable prompt prefixes and cache-reusing forks so cross-session memory adds almost no token cost.
items.whyItMatters: A concrete way to push routine coding-agent cost toward zero via DeepSeek's cache pricing while staying compatible with your existing Skills/MCP/Hooks config.
items.tryThis: Clone tigicion/dao-code, wire in a DeepSeek-V4 API key, and reuse your existing Claude Code Skills/Hooks.

items.title: Javis603/token-monitor — Local-first desktop widget for tracking token usage, costs, and limits across 28+ AI coding tools—including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and OpenClaw—with multi-device sync.
items.tldr: token-monitor is a local-first desktop widget tracking token usage, cost and limits across 28+ AI coding tools including Claude Code and Codex, with multi-device sync.
items.whyItMatters: Gives real visibility into what unattended runs actually cost instead of checking each provider dashboard separately.
items.tryThis: Install Javis603/token-monitor to watch Claude Code and Codex spend across overnight runs.

items.title: withkynam/vibecode-pro-max-kit — Your AI forgets. This remembers. Spec-driven coding harness for vibecoders, product owners, CEOs and real builders — self-improving context memory, 15 agents, 33 skills working with /goal, agent-team, & work
items.tldr: vibecode-pro-max-kit is a spec-driven Claude Code/Codex harness with 15 agents and 33 skills built around a /goal command and workflow autopilot loops meant to run with no human gate.
items.whyItMatters: Targets exactly his describe-it-and-sleep goal — worth testing whether the autopilot loop really avoids mid-run questions.
items.tryThis: Clone withkynam/vibecode-pro-max-kit and run /goal on a small feature to see how far the autopilot loop gets unattended.

items.title: CodeBendKit/codeseek — Rust-powered code intelligence CLI for AI coding agents. Builds call graphs and hybrid semantic search indexes (Dense + Sparse + RRF + Reranker) across 7 languages. Ships as native MCP tools for Claude Code and Codex
items.tldr: codeseek is a Rust CLI that builds call graphs and hybrid semantic/sparse search indexes across 7 languages, shipped as native MCP tools for Claude Code and Codex CLI.
items.whyItMatters: Better repo-level context retrieval means fewer clarifying questions from an agent mid-task.
items.tryThis: Add CodeBendKit/codeseek as an MCP server in your Claude Code config so subagents get call-graph and semantic search instead of grepping blind.

items.title: razzant/claudexor — Multi-harness control plane for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode: quota-aware rotation across multiple Claude/Codex subscriptions, shared thread context, and cross-model review.
items.tldr: claudexor is a control plane doing quota-aware rotation across multiple Claude/Codex subscriptions, with shared thread context and cross-model review.
items.whyItMatters: Directly solves an overnight run dying mid-way from a quota wall, and adds free cross-model PR review as a side effect.
items.tryThis: Point claudexor at your Claude and Codex subscriptions so long runs auto-rotate before hitting a quota wall.

items.title: AirLLM 70B inference with single 4GB GPU
items.tldr: AirLLM runs 70B-parameter model inference on a single 4GB GPU by streaming layers instead of holding the whole model in VRAM.
items.whyItMatters: Puts a 70B-class model within reach of consumer hardware you already own, for offline or throwaway subagent work with zero API cost.
items.tryThis: Clone AirLLM and try a 70B model on your 4GB+ GPU for slow-but-free background tasks that don't need Claude-tier speed.

items.title: Homebench – Benchmark local LLMs for speed, memory, and quality
items.tldr: Homebench is a new open-source tool for benchmarking local LLMs on speed, memory footprint, and output quality on your own machine.
items.whyItMatters: Lets you measure which local/open-weight model actually fits your laptop before routing cheap subagent work to it, instead of trusting vendor benchmarks.
items.tryThis: Clone Homebench and run it against candidate local models on your dev machine to pick one for background/verification subagents.

items.title: omnigent-ai/omnigent — Omnigent is an open-source AI agent framework and meta-harness: orchestrate Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and custom agents — swap harnesses without rewriting, enforce policies and sandboxing, and collaborate in rea
items.tldr: Omnigent is an open-source meta-harness that orchestrates Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Pi under one policy/sandbox layer and lets you collaborate on running agents from any device.
items.whyItMatters: Gives a path to check on or steer overnight agent runs from a phone without building a bespoke bridge.
items.tryThis: Clone omnigent-ai/omnigent and put it in front of your existing Claude Code sessions for remote/mobile visibility.

items.title: oomol-lab/open-connector — Open-source auth gateway connecting 1000+ SaaS providers to AI agents through SDK, CLI, MCP, HTTP, and OpenAPI.
items.tldr: open-connector is an open-source auth gateway that wires 1000+ SaaS providers into AI agents via SDK, CLI, MCP, HTTP, and OpenAPI.
items.whyItMatters: Gives your coding agent a single MCP-compatible gateway to real SaaS accounts instead of hand-writing auth for each integration.
items.tryThis: Point your agent's MCP config at open-connector to gate SaaS access instead of maintaining per-service API key plumbing.

items.title: Waishnav/devspace — Turn ChatGPT into Codex! OR Turn Claude Web into Claude Code!
items.tldr: devspace turns a ChatGPT or Claude web session into a Codex/Claude-Code-style CLI agent, at 3,527 stars.
items.whyItMatters: Potentially lets some agentic coding run through a flat-rate web subscription instead of metered API calls.
items.tryThis: Clone Waishnav/devspace and test it on a low-stakes task to see how much API spend it actually replaces.

items.title: larlarua/AutoCVE — Agent-driven automated CVE discovery platform for source code auditing, vulnerability verification, and report generation.
items.tldr: AutoCVE is an agent-driven platform that automates CVE discovery, verification, and report generation on source code.
items.whyItMatters: This is a droppable security-audit stage he could wire into a review hook or subagent so vulnerable code gets flagged before he wakes up to review the PR.
items.tryThis: Clone larlarua/AutoCVE and run it as a pre-review pass on agent-generated diffs to catch vulnerabilities before merge.

items.title: scasella/claude-dynamic-workflows-codex — Run Claude Code dynamic workflows on a local Codex (GPT) backend, plus an interactive run viewer
items.tldr: claude-dynamic-workflows-codex runs Claude Code's dynamic workflow engine on a local Codex/GPT backend, with an interactive run viewer.
items.whyItMatters: The run viewer gives a lightweight way to inspect what an unattended workflow actually did before opening the PR.
items.tryThis: Clone scasella/claude-dynamic-workflows-codex, swap one workflow to a local Codex backend, and check its run viewer output.

items.title: Smaller, faster, safer: running Kimi and GLM at scale
items.tldr: Post details running Kimi and GLM open-weight models at scale more cheaply and safely than closed frontier models.
items.whyItMatters: Kimi and GLM are viable self-hosted or cheap-API targets for offloading routine subagent tasks away from your Claude Code spend.
items.tryThis: Check whether a Kimi or GLM endpoint can take your cheap/background subagent calls instead of a paid frontier model.

items.title: Launch HN: Hoplite (YC S26) – Effortlessly deploy cloud coding agents
items.tldr: Hoplite (YC S26) launches a cloud deployment tool that imports your local coding-agent setup — sessions, memory, MCP servers — and runs it in the cloud for QA.
items.whyItMatters: A ready path to run and QA agent sessions off your laptop instead of hand-building your own remote/cloud harness.
items.tryThis: Check hoplite.sh's onboarding to port your Claude Code sessions/MCP servers into a cloud run.

clusters.title: Fable's verification workflow ported into Claude Code skills
clusters.summary: Two separate repos this cycle distill Anthropic's internal Fable think/act/prove approach into a portable skill plus eval, aimed at making an agent prove its work before calling a task complete.

clusters.title: Cheaper backends for routine agent work
clusters.summary: A run of tools lets you route subagent work off paid frontier APIs: a universal provider proxy, a DeepSeek-V4-tuned agent with cache-reusing prefixes, a way to run 70B models on a 4GB GPU, and a benchmark to pick the right local model first.

clusters.title: Running agents off your laptop
clusters.summary: Two new harness/cloud tools aim at supervising or executing coding-agent sessions away from your machine rather than just locally.
